fields.about:
I'm an M.Tech student in Information Technology at NIT Raipur, working at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, machine learning research, and software engineering. My current thesis focuses on deepfake detection under adversarial attacks using Agentic AI, where I build a trust-aware multi-agent system combining texture, frequency, semantic, and robustness analysis to improve detection reliability against sophisticated attacks.

I enjoy working on problems where research meets practical engineering. From building a 6M-parameter Transformer from scratch for narrative consistency verification to developing multimodal price prediction systems using deep learning and ensemble models, I focus on understanding how models work, evaluating them rigorously, and turning them into usable applications.

I primarily work with Python, C++, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Django, and Transformers. My interests span deep learning, computer vision, NLP, RAG systems, adversarial machine learning, and full-stack development. I also have industry experience as a Data Science Intern at APSSDC, where I developed an NLP-based sentiment analysis model achieving 88% accuracy.

Beyond academics, I qualified GATE 2025 and served as General Secretary of the SGC Lecture Series Club, coordinating technical events, workshops, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

fields.title: Doc Generator App
fields.subtitle: Schema-driven document generation on the Google Workspace APIs
fields.short_description: A full-stack platform that generates documents from reusable Google Docs templates, using dynamic JSON field schemas so new document types need no code changes.
fields.description:
Most document generators hardcode one template per document type. This one treats the schema as data: a JSON field definition describes the placeholders, so adding a new document type is a configuration change rather than a deployment.
Google OAuth2 handles authentication, the Docs API's batchUpdate performs placeholder replacement in a single call, and the Drive API manages access and export.
fields.highlights:
Schema-driven design supporting unlimited document types
Google OAuth2 authentication end to end
Docs API batchUpdate for atomic placeholder replacement
Drive API integration for document access and export
fields.tech_stack: Django, Django REST Framework, Google Docs API, Google Drive API, OAuth2, Python

fields.title: Retrieval-Augmented Narrative Consistency Verification
fields.subtitle: A 10.7M-parameter Transformer trained from scratch
fields.short_description: A BERT-style Transformer paired with a hybrid BM25 and semantic retrieval RAG pipeline, verifying whether narrative statements stay consistent with their source text.
fields.description:
The encoder was designed and trained from scratch at 10.7M parameters rather than fine-tuned from a checkpoint, so every architectural choice could be measured independently.
Retrieval combines lexical BM25 with dense semantic search — each finds evidence the other misses, and the combination moved accuracy more than any single modelling change.
fields.highlights:
97.56% accuracy on the verification task
0.97 Macro F1 and 0.99 ROC-AUC
Hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval for evidence selection
10.7M-parameter encoder trained from scratch
fields.tech_stack: PyTorch, Transformers, RAG, BM25, NLP, Python

fields.title: AI-Powered Multimodal E-commerce Price Prediction System
fields.subtitle: Product text and images feeding a stacked ensemble
fields.short_description: An end-to-end system predicting product prices from both descriptions and images, served through a Streamlit app for real-time predictions and automated reporting.
fields.description:
Textual features cover keywords, quality indicators and numeric analysis of the listing copy; deep image features come from pre-trained MobileNetV2 and ResNet50 backbones.
Predictions come from a super ensemble of XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and Ridge Regression, wrapped in a Streamlit interface with automated reporting.

Five-model stacked ensemble for the final prediction
Streamlit app for real-time pricing and reports

fields.title: Agentic Deepfake Detection under Adversarial Attacks
fields.subtitle: A trust-aware multi-agent system that keeps detecting deepfakes when attackers add invisible noise to fool the detector
fields.short_description: Deepfake video detection that stays reliable under adversarial attacks. It uses three forensic agents, a trust-checking robustness agent and a Transformer coordinator.
fields.description: Deepfake detectors work well on normal videos, but invisible adversarial noise can fool them completely. This research builds an agentic system that resists such attacks. Three agents examine different evidence: texture (GenD-CLIP features and SRM noise), frequency (DCT, FFT and phase patterns) and motion (an R(2+1)D video network). A robustness agent cleans each video and re-checks it, to measure how far each agent can be trusted and to raise an attack alarm. A Transformer coordinator combines the agents by confidence and trust and decides Real, Fake or Uncertain. It never says Real while an attack is detected. An explainability agent shows heat-maps, frequency views, motion maps and a plain-language trust report. The system is evaluated on FaceForensics++ against black-box, white-box and fully adaptive attackers.
fields.highlights:
Reproduced and stress-tested GenD (WACV 2026) under adversarial attacks
Three forensic agents: texture, frequency and motion
Trust-based robustness agent with an attack alarm
Transformer coordinator with Real / Fake / Uncertain decisions
Adversarial training with FGSM and PGD
Explainability: heat-maps, frequency views and trust reports
Evaluated against black-box, white-box and adaptive attacks

fields.title: Why schema-driven beats one-template-per-document
fields.excerpt: The first version of my document generator needed a code change for every new document type. The second one didn't.
fields.body:
The obvious way to build a document generator is one template, one handler, one endpoint. It works beautifully until someone asks for a fourth document type and you realise you've written the same function three times.

The version I ended up with treats the schema as data. A JSON field definition describes what placeholders a template has and what each one expects. Adding a document type means adding a row, not writing and deploying a handler.

The Google Docs API rewards this design. Its batchUpdate endpoint takes a list of replacement operations and applies them in one call, so a schema with twenty placeholders costs exactly as much as one with two. Combined with OAuth2 for access and the Drive API for export, the whole pipeline stays under a few hundred lines.

fields.title: BM25 and embeddings find different things
fields.excerpt: I assumed dense retrieval would make keyword search redundant. Measuring it changed my mind.
fields.body:
When I started the narrative consistency project I expected semantic search to dominate. Embeddings understand meaning; keyword matching is the thing embeddings were invented to replace.

That isn't what the retrieval logs showed. BM25 reliably caught exact names, numbers and rare terms that embeddings smoothed into their neighbours. Dense search caught paraphrases that shared no vocabulary with the query at all. Each method's failures were the other's successes.

Combining them was worth more than any change I made to the model itself. The final system reached 97.56% accuracy with a 0.99 ROC-AUC, and most of the distance from the baseline came from what the retriever put in front of the encoder rather than the encoder's own capacity.
